PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.
FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

### BACKGROUND
State Corporate Income Taxes.
...
Multistate Businesses Choose How Their Taxable Income Is Determined.
Currently, state law allows most multistate businesses to pick one of two methods to determine the amount of their income associated with California and taxable by the state:
- “Three-Factor Method” of Determining Taxable Income.
One method uses the location of the company’s sales, property, and employees.
When using this method, the more sales, property, or employees the multistate business has in California, the more of the business’ income is subject to state tax.
- “Single Sales Factor Method” of Determining Taxable Income.
The other method uses only the location of the company’s sales.
When using this method, the more sales the multistate business has in California, the more of the business’ income is taxed.

PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. YES

NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.

PRO

Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

## Proposition 39: Prohibits Citizens From Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
### Summary
Proposition 39 began as a citizen-initiated constitutional amendment filed with the California Attorney General's office on July 16, 2025.
The initiative received a revised ballot title and was approved for signature gathering on September 19, 2025.
To qualify for the ballot, proponents were required to collect 874,641 valid signatures.The campaign submitted nearly 1.37 million signatures on March 2, 2026 and the initiative officially qualified for the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 39 on April 24, 2026.
On July 27, 2026, Californians for Voter ID filed a lawsuit against the Secretary of State challenging the new ballot title for Proposition 39, which was drafted by Attorney General Rob Bonta after his office received the amendment.
The plaintiffs argued that the new title of “prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification,” was false and misleading, as it did not include the original title’s reference to additional voter identification and citizenship verification requirements.
The Attorney General’s Office maintained that the revised language more accurately describes the measure’s provisions.

***Requires Voters to Select Government-Issued Identification for Voting by Mail.*** Proposition 39 requires new and existing voters to select a government-issued identification in their voter registration to vote by mail.
***Requires Voters to Provide Additional Identifying Information to Vote.*** Proposition 39 requires voters to provide additional identifying information each time they cast a ballot in any election in California.
Elections officials would be required to verify voters’ identities before counting their ballots.
The identification requirement would depend on whether a voter casts their ballot in person or by mail:
- ***In-Person Voting.*** When voting in person, Proposition 39 requires voters to present government-issued identification for identity verification.
- ***Voting by Mail.*** When voting by mail, Proposition 39 requires voters to provide the last four digits of their selected government-issued identification number on the ballot envelope.

The SurveyUSA poll found that 49% support the measure, 42% are against it, and 10% are undecided.
A news release published with the poll pointed out that opposition tends to rise as elections near and that support for the measure has dipped from last month, when support was 48% and opposition was 38%, making for a 10-point difference.
The PPIC poll found even less support for requiring IDs to vote in California, with 41% of respondents saying they plan to vote yes and 58% planning to vote no.

## Proposition 39: Prohibits Citizens From Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
### Summary
Proposition 39 began as a citizen-initiated constitutional amendment filed with the California Attorney General's office on July 16, 2025.
The initiative received a revised ballot title and was approved for signature gathering on September 19, 2025.
To qualify for the ballot, proponents were required to collect 874,641 valid signatures.The campaign submitted nearly 1.37 million signatures on March 2, 2026 and the initiative officially qualified for the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 39 on April 24, 2026.
On July 27, 2026, Californians for Voter ID filed a lawsuit against the Secretary of State challenging the new ballot title for Proposition 39, which was drafted by Attorney General Rob Bonta after his office received the amendment.
The plaintiffs argued that the new title of “prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification,” was false and misleading, as it did not include the original title’s reference to additional voter identification and citizenship verification requirements.
The Attorney General’s Office maintained that the revised language more accurately describes the measure’s provisions.

Californians are being asked to vote 'yes' or 'no' on 14 ballot measures.
One of them is Proposition 39, which, according to the Legislative Analyst's Office, would require election officials to verify Californians' U.S. citizenship and prohibit them from voting without a government-issued ID.
It also creates other rules around the voting process and identity verification when voting in person vs. by mail and ongoing compliance checks.
Voting 'yes' would mean that you need to present a government-issued ID to vote in person and if you're voting by mail, you need to provide the last four digits of that ID.

Californians are being asked to vote 'yes' or 'no' on 14 ballot measures.
One of them is Proposition 39, which, according to the Legislative Analyst's Office, would require election officials to verify Californians' U.S. citizenship and prohibit them from voting without a government-issued ID.
It also creates other rules around the voting process and identity verification when voting in person vs. by mail and ongoing compliance checks.
Voting 'yes' would mean that you need to present a government-issued ID to vote in person and if you're voting by mail, you need to provide the last four digits of that ID.
Voting 'no' means the process stays is it is — you don't need to present an ID to vote and your citizenship is verified during the registration process.

39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

### Summary
Proposition 39 began as a citizen-initiated constitutional amendment filed with the California Attorney General's office on July 16, 2025.
The initiative received a revised ballot title and was approved for signature gathering on September 19, 2025.
To qualify for the ballot, proponents were required to collect 874,641 valid signatures.The campaign submitted nearly 1.37 million signatures on March 2, 2026 and the initiative officially qualified for the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 39 on April 24, 2026.

Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents whose net worth exceeds $1 billion.

Taxpayers could opt to pay the tax, due in 2027, over five years, but would have to pay more.
Ninety percent of the revenue would go to health care programs, while the remaining 10% would go to education and food assistance programs.
Two countermeasures to the proposed wealth tax, Propositions 41 and 42, have also qualified for the November ballot.
The initiatives are intended to limit the effects of Proposition 40 if voters approve it.
